Definition: from G3144; to be a witness, i.e. testify (literally or figuratively):--charge, give (evidence), bear record, have (obtain, of) good (honest) report, be well reported of, testify, give (have) testimony, (be, bear, give, obtain) witness.
BiblicalUsage: martyréō is to bear witness, to testify, and it carries the weight of the whole New Testament. In 1 John 1:2 the apostles have seen the life manifested and bear witness and show it, and in 1 John 4:14 they testify that the Father sent the Son to be the Saviour of the world. In 1 Corinthians 15:15 Paul says the apostles would be false witnesses of God if Christ were not raised, and in 1 John 5:6 the Spirit bears witness because the Spirit is truth. Witness here is sworn testimony, not opinion.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe martyréō teaches me that a witness is not a debater but someone who has seen. I hold that my testimony stands or falls on what I have seen of Christ.
